solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Classify large mammal

blocks.note: to rate something is to grade or classify it
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like 'classify a large mammal', but 'large' is only its abbreviation and the definition is just 'mammal'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel is the honey badger, a fierce African and Asian carnivore, so it is one example of a mammal.

clue.text: Mistake wearing jewel that’s cheap?

indicators.note: whatever is worn is carried around something, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a ruby is a red gemstone
bish is informal British slang for a blunder

explanation.surface: Someone has made the error of wearing a gaudy jewel that looks cheap.
explanation.walkthrough: The jewel does the wearing, not a person; the mistake is a chiefly British slang word, bish, for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shoddy and worthless is trashy, of poor quality, which is what cheap means as an insult.

clue.text: Dances taking you most of the way to heaven?

blocks.clueFragment: taking you most of the way to heaven?
blocks.note: surface reading: something that nearly gets you to paradise

blocks.clueFragment: taking you most of the way to heaven?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the song 'Three Steps to Heaven' means a pair of paces covers most of the distance

explanation.walkthrough: Eddie Cochran's hit 'Three Steps to Heaven' says three paces get you there; a pair of them therefore takes you most of the way.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-step is a ballroom and country dance in duple time, so the plural names several such dances.

clue.text: For those attending Royal gala: wine isn’t one I’d fancy!

indicators.note: to fancy is to imagine or invent, so the letters are reworked into something new

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A guest at a royal gala sniffs at the wine on offer: not one they would choose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb of liking at the end of a complaint, but it is the anagram signal; 'one' adds a single I to the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies-in-waiting are noblewomen who serve as personal attendants to a queen or princess at court.

clue.text: Saw lagers being put out in this?

definitions.text: Saw lagers being put out in this?

indicators.note: something put out is displaced or disturbed, so these letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone watched beers being set out on the bar in some kind of container.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the letters of the first two words are rearranged, and the full sentence describes what beer is served in.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasses, tankards and jugs are the vessels in which pints of beer are set out for drinkers.

clue.text: Fellow colonel gasps, lifting exhibits

indicators.note: to exhibit is to put on show, so the answer is displayed within the words
in a down clue lifting lets the letters read upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A fellow officer gasps as he lifts some objects on display.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidden in 'colonel gasps' as NELG, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow is a man, and Glen is a man's first name, a standard crossword way of defining given names.

clue.text: Looking for what we have broadcast late

indicators.note: a broadcast is sent out over the air to be listened to, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: to be after something is to be seeking it
what belongs to us is ours, and spoken it matches a word for periods of time

explanation.surface: Someone is searching for a programme we have that goes out late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast late' reads as a late-night show, but 'late' is the definition and 'broadcast' only turns OURS into the sound of HOURS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done after hours happens past normal opening or working time, which is late in the day.

clue.text: Not entirely clear, possibly, father of Irishman’s eaten most of joint

indicators.note: most of a thing is all but a little of it, so the final letter goes
what is eaten goes inside the eater, so one piece is swallowed by another

blocks.note: Sean is a typical Irish name, plus the possessive S
a mitre is a carpentry joint, less its last letter
a father is a parent

explanation.surface: An Irish father, not quite thinking clearly, has polished off most of the roast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests a roast, but it is the carpenter's mitre joint, two pieces cut at an angle to meet at a corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A semitransparent material lets some light through but blurs it, so it is only partly clear, perhaps.

clue.text: Don’t get on / like a house on fire?

blocks.note: first meaning: step down from a bus or train rather than boarding it
second meaning: burning, in flames

explanation.walkthrough: Together the words suggest the idiom about people who get on famously, which is the opposite of not getting on; each half is really a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to get off a vehicle, and a house on fire is burning, which is also meant by this word.

clue.text: Body: it’s what was right inside doorway

indicators.note: to be what something was is to take over its place, so one letter is swapped for another
inside locates the swap within a longer word rather than at an end

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
an entry is a way in, a doorway

explanation.surface: A body is found in the doorway, and someone explains what used to be there.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as a statement of replacement: the pronoun now sits where the abbreviation for right used to be in the doorway word.
explanation.definitionFit: A body in the sense of an organisation or a distinct thing is an entity, something with separate existence.

clue.text: Reddest stain, in which nothing fades

indicators.note: something with things in it holds them, so it wraps around the other pieces

blocks.note: a blot is a stain
O looks like zero
a sound or light that fades dies away

explanation.surface: The reddest stain of all is one that never fades away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fades' is not the stain losing colour but a verb meaning passes away, and it goes inside with nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloody can mean covered in or coloured like blood, so the superlative is the most intensely red.

clue.text: Man pulling back stone getting sweaty?

indicators.note: pulling back draws something the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the Isle of Man, abbreviated IOM
ST is the abbreviation for stone, a British unit of weight of 14 pounds

explanation.surface: A man heaving a heavy stone backwards is working up a sweat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man, whose abbreviation IOM turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin that is sweaty is damp with perspiration, and damp is a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Interested by journalist with abnormally shaped feet

blocks.note: to be into something is to be keen on it
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A reader takes an interest in a reporter who has oddly formed feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interested by' sounds like a passive phrase, but the informal 'into' is the first piece and ED, the editor, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in-toed has toes that turn inwards, a condition also called pigeon-toed, a deformity of the foot.

clue.text: Cross, but not quite to the end, note

indicators.note: stopping just short of the finish drops the final letter

blocks.note: crotchety means irritable, bad-tempered

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed by a note, but not all the way through reading it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' is the adjective meaning angry, not a mark or a verb; CROTCHETY loses its Y.
explanation.definitionFit: In British musical terminology a crotchet is a quarter note, one beat in common time, so it is a note.

clue.text: Roughly chopping stick in preparation for working with trap

blocks.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
hewing is cutting with an axe
gum is glue, something to stick with

explanation.surface: A woodworker roughly chops a stick, getting it ready to use with a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trap' is slang for the mouth, and 'preparation' is a made-up substance, not getting ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum is a sweet substance made to be chewed, so it is a product meant for the jaws to work on.

clue.text: Greeting quietly? In house, men always cheer

blocks.note: hi is a greeting
P is piano, the musical direction to play softly
in and hip both mean fashionable
HO is the abbreviation for house
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
ay, or aye, is an old word for ever

explanation.surface: A soft greeting is followed by the men of the house raising a constant cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition placing things inside the house, but it means fashionable and gives the second HIP.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the traditional shout of three rousing cries given in celebration, so it is a cheer.

clue.text: American chasing game however claims to work hard

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: but and however both introduce a contrast
US is short for United States
tag is the playground game where one player chases the others

explanation.surface: An American playing a pursuit game insists that he is putting in a lot of effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chasing' looks like it orders the pieces, but it belongs with 'game' to describe the playground game.
explanation.definitionFit: To bust a gut is an informal idiom for straining yourself, making an enormous effort at a task.

clue.text: Publicity over animal sanctuary scandal upset rider

indicators.note: something upset is turned over, and in a down clue that flips the letters to read upwards

blocks.note: an ad is an advertisement, publicity
a den is an animal's lair, its refuge
mud is scandalous gossip, as in mudslinging

explanation.surface: Press coverage of a scandal at an animal refuge has upset a horse rider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' is not someone on a horse but a clause added to a document, and 'over' simply stacks the first piece on top in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is an extra clause attached to a bill or contract, and an addendum is likewise something appended.

clue.text: Revolting group of children under guard after week occupying a playground?

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to be inside it, so these letters sit within another piece
coming after means following, so the preceding piece is placed second

blocks.note: taken as written
WK is the abbreviation for week
wards are young people under a guardian's protection
a quad is a school or college courtyard used for play

explanation.surface: Rebellious kids, watched by a guard, have taken over the playground for a week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' means rebellious, not disgusting; a quad is a quadrangle, a courtyard enclosed by school or college buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: An awkward squad is a collection of people who obstruct or rebel against authority, a group in revolt.

clue.text: Spirit nobody in large organisation is able to raise

indicators.note: raising something lifts it, and in a down clue that makes the letters read upwards

blocks.note: an unimportant person in a big machine is a mere cog
can means is able

explanation.surface: An insignificant employee in a big firm still has the spirit to rise up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' reads as morale, but it is a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a French brandy, and brandy is a distilled alcoholic drink, a spirit.

clue.text: Cancel gun permit on tip from police

indicators.note: a tip is an extreme end, so only one letter at the finish is kept

blocks.note: to gun an engine is to rev it
to OK something is to permit it
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Following a tip-off from the police, a firearms licence is withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gun' and 'permit' are verbs, not a weapon and a licence; the police tip is the last letter, not the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To revoke a licence or order is to withdraw it officially, so it is a synonym of cancel.

clue.text: Disposed, ie, to bend?

indicators.note: things disposed are arranged or set out, so these letters are placed in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A definition-like note: inclined, that is, to give way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposed' rearranges the other letters, and the whole phrase also defines the answer: someone disposed to bend to others' will.
explanation.definitionFit: A compliant person is inclined to yield and submit to orders, which is exactly being willing to bend.

clue.text: Put out / toy

blocks.note: first meaning: fluster, unsettle someone
second meaning: a baby's plaything that clatters when shaken

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' can mean extinguish or set out, but here it means disconcerted, as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle someone is to make them nervous and irritated, and a baby's noisy plaything goes by the same word.

clue.text: Strategy the board has failed to complete

indicators.note: failing to finish leaves the ending off, so the last letter is lost

blocks.note: a plank is a board of wood

explanation.surface: A company's board has failed to finish drawing up its strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The board' looks like a company's directors, but it is a piece of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a scheme worked out in advance for achieving an aim, which is what a strategy is.

clue.text: Miss, possibly, I lament on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things backwards, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: taken as written
to moan is to lament

explanation.surface: Someone who has missed out, perhaps, grieves over it after thinking it through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' is a title for an unmarried woman, not a failure; 'possibly' warns that any girl's name will do.
explanation.definitionFit: A Miss is a girl or young woman, and Naomi is one example of a female first name.

clue.text: Top quality speaker’s self-reproach was slow to shift

indicators.note: what belongs to a speaker is spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: blaming yourself is feeling guilt, which is heard like gold plating
to edge is to move gradually and cautiously

explanation.surface: A top-class orator, full of remorse, was reluctant to change position.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first half is a sound-alike; the second piece is spelt as it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilt-edged originally described safe government stocks and now means of the highest reliability and quality.

clue.text: Priest leading female PE disturbs family

indicators.note: something that disturbs breaks in on another, so these letters interrupt the next piece

blocks.note: a clan is an extended family
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen, the chief woman in the land
PE, physical education, is also called gym

explanation.surface: A cleric at the front of a women's exercise class upsets the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' seems to put the priest in front, but 'leading female' is the Queen, the standard crossword ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman is a male member of the Christian clergy, of which a priest is one kind.

clue.text: Exchange of tips on choral composition’s symbol

indicators.note: trading tips means swapping the two ends, so the first and last letters change places

blocks.note: a motet is a short sacred piece for voices

explanation.surface: Singers trade advice about the meaning of a symbol in a choral work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' looks like advice, but it means the ends of the word, which trade places.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or animal revered as the emblem of a clan, so it serves as a symbol.
